fichas.title: Relationship between duties and room type
fichas.summary: The diagram relates office tasks to types of work and locations. Routine tasks are associated with individual work in a single room; project development and meetings or negotiations connect to team work, exchange, group rooms, and meeting rooms.

fichas.title: Office area included in calculation of rent according to GIF
fichas.summary: The diagram divides office area included in rent calculations into main usable area, subsidiary areas, and partly proportional traffic areas. The accompanying note describes GIF definitions for rented office and commercial areas, developed with the DIN standards committee for comparing commercial rents. Shared-use areas are considered proportionally; application is not binding.
uses: Classifying areas for commercial rent calculations

fichas.title: Organisational structure of office space
fichas.summary: The diagram organizes office space from total gross area and building-related area into net office area and net special area. It distinguishes workgroup-related office areas, service and traffic areas, technical supply and structural areas, and specially protected office-related areas. Further categories describe functional workplace space, usable space for workgroups, and special usable space for workgroups, alongside considerations such as access, privacy, noise reduction, and visitor traffic.

fichas.title: Factors determining office work
fichas.summary: The diagram groups determinants of office work into performance, organisation, equipment, and working conditions, with endogenous and exogenous forces also influencing office planning. Listed considerations include employee needs, organisational procedures, office equipment, acoustics, lighting, room types, flexibility, economic conditions, and technology.
uses: Planning office organization and working conditions

fichas.title: Office work and design
fichas.summary: Office work is shifting from routine data processing toward creative information processing and evaluation. Employee performance, corporate identity, break and relaxation areas, and individual workplace configuration are emphasized. Global networking supports decentralized routine work, while headquarters increasingly function as shared information marketplaces for employees working temporarily or in changing groups. Office buildings therefore need adaptable spaces, ranging from single offices and group rooms to intermittently used workstations such as hot desking. Design begins with recording business organization, functions, and working relationships to establish requirements; rented buildings benefit from flexible layouts that allow variable office-unit sizes.
